section.title: Additional topics: Richardson and Romberg methods

introduction.p: When an approximation has a known leading error term in the step size, two mesh sizes can be combined to cancel that term. This optional section derives Richardson extrapolation and applies it repeatedly to the trapezoidal rule to obtain Romberg integration. The improved orders require the stated error expansion and sufficient smoothness.

subsection.title: Repeated extrapolation of trapezoidal rules
subsection.p: For a sufficiently smooth function on [a,b], the composite trapezoidal rule has an expansion in even powers of its uniform mesh width:

One sufficient condition for this expansion through the displayed order is that f have 2m+2 continuous derivatives on the interval. It comes from Taylor expansion on the panels and summing their endpoint contributions. The first coefficient is c_2=(f'(b)-f'(a))/12; symmetry removes the odd powers. This expansion is stronger information than the trapezoidal error bound alone.
Let h_k=(b-a)/2^k. Set R_{k,0}=T(h_k) and form the triangular Romberg table by

Column j cancels the leading error of order h^{2j} from the preceding column. For fixed j and sufficient smoothness, its error is O(h_k^{2j+2}) as the mesh shrinks. Finite-precision diagonal entries need not improve at every refinement.
Each refinement reuses previous function values:
Only the newly inserted midpoints are evaluated. The first extrapolated column is exactly the composite Simpson rule on that grid: R_{k,1}=(4T(h_k)-T(2h_k))/3.

example.title: An exactly checkable table
example.p: For f(x)=x^4 on [0,1], I=1/5 and direct finite summation gives T(h)=1/5+h^2/3-h^4/30.
The second extrapolation cancels the h^4 term, leaving the exact integral in exact arithmetic.

paragraphs.title: A practical stopping policy
paragraphs.p: Choose a tolerance \tau=\tau_{\rm abs}+\tau_{\rm rel}|R_{k,k}| with \tau_{\rm abs}>0, \tau_{\rm rel}\ge0. One policy requires at least three refinements and two consecutive diagonal changes below the current tolerance. Also impose a maximum refinement level and function-evaluation budget, reject nonfinite values, and stop with a failure report if the mesh cannot be represented or the changes cease decreasing while the tolerance is unmet. Report the latest diagonal change as an estimate, not a certified bound. A known derivative bound or other rigorous remainder estimate is needed for a certified stopping decision.

warning.title: The expansion has hypotheses
warning.p: For f(x)=\sqrt{x} on [0,1], derivatives blow up at zero and the usual even-power expansion is unavailable. Applying the Romberg recurrence is still possible, but the advertised orders no longer follow. Increasing the table depth cannot repair an unjustified error model.

statement.p: If A(h)=I+ch^3+O(h^4), find the Richardson combination. Build the first three Romberg rows for \int_0^1x^2\,dx. Which column first gives the exact result, and why?

hint.p: Use (8A(h/2)-A(h))/7. For the quadratic, T(h)=1/3+h^2/6, so the first extrapolated column is exact.
